messages:
amber-cs: Customer BrightShip reporting repeated 5xx and long tail latency from hosted inference in ap-southeast1 since ~04:00 UTC. Symptoms: intermittent 502 gateway errors, auth retries, and some requests hanging 10-30s. Providing sample req ids and repro.

kevin-sre: thanks Amber — can you paste a sample curl + request ids and customer repro steps? I'll pull traces for that time window.

amber-cs: sample repro (customer):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}'
```
Sample request ids: req=1a2b3c4d, req=1a2b3c4e, req=1a2b3c4f. Customer saw repeated 502 + TLS handshake errors in client logs.

kevin-sre: pulled gateway logs. Seeing upstream ECONNRESET and TLS handshake timeouts matching those req ids. Also large spike in auth retry counts. Tracing path now.

sara-net: I see egress BGP withdraws toward provider APAC-Transit (ASN 64501) — neighbor 203.0.113.5 flapping to peer. Resulting in asymmetric routing: some flows hairpin to upstream and come back same AZ over different provider. Packet loss ~1-2% and reordering spikes at same window. Correlates exactly with your timestamps.

monitoring-bot: ALERT hosted-api.ap-southeast1.gateway.5xx rate +350% (2026-03-15T04:03:00Z). auth.retry.count doubled.

kevin-sre: hypothesis: hairpin/asymmetric egress increases RTT and causes KV cache miss + connection timeouts -> 502s and auth token refresh races. Mitigations to try:
1) steer egress away from flapping provider for affected prefixes
2) temporarily reroute customer traffic to secondary peer regionally
3) increase upstream connect timeout for in-flight requests to avoid dropping active connections

sara-net: applying routing changes now. I'll add community 64501:666 to prefer peer-2 for 203.0.113.0/24 and enable dampening adjustments to smooth withdraws. Pushing route-map in 3-5 min.

amber-cs: passing update to BrightShip: "We are applying network-level steering. Expect intermittent improvement in the next 5-15 minutes. We'll confirm."

maria-support: I DM'ed the customer and included our mitigation plan + ETA. They asked for an RFC/ticket. Filed case with customer contact and will follow with provider ticket ID once we have it.

deploy-bot: Routing override committed: region=ap-southeast1 commit=3f9a7e route-map=steer-away-203-0-113

sara-net: telemetry after change: packet loss on egress prefix down from 1.8% -> 0.2%, reordering reduced. BGP flap count dropped.

kevin-sre: rechecked gateway logs and retried customer repro curl. Now returning 200s. Example log: `2026-03-15T04:16:12Z req=1a2b3c4d status=200 latency=210ms` (previously failed). Auth retry counters back to baseline.

amber-cs: BrightShip confirmed their tests are green and latency returned to normal. They appreciate the quick action.

maria-support: Opening follow-up with transit provider: ticket #AS-2026-759 created (includes pcap/traces, timestamps, and AS path snapshots). Sharing with provider ops and asking for root cause and permanent mitigation.

kevin-sre: follow-ups for us:
- add a prom alert to detect AS path hairpin/asymmetry for egress ASNs
- add a canary for KV cache warm after failover to avoid cold-cache tail latency
- document runbook steps for egress-steering and customer comms

amber-cs: thanks everyone — closure confirmed from customer :thumbsup:. Will add notes to incident log and hand to postmortem.

sara-net: adding final note: removed temporary community in 2 hours after provider confirmed they stabilized links; will update peer config once ticket completes.

kevin-sre: moving to post-incident follow-up. Good job on quick mitigation and customer comms.
